concepts.name: Bit complexity
concepts.gloss: The running time of an algorithm measured as the number of elementary bit-level steps on a fixed machine model, as opposed to arithmetic operations on words.

evidence.quote: the algorithm is intended to establish a bit-complexity bound

concepts.name: Centred extraction
concepts.gloss: Recovering each packed coefficient as the representative in a window centred at zero, so that a signed coefficient is not confused with a large positive one.

evidence.quote: Signed packing, centered extraction, negacyclic wrapping, and copying are linear stream passes

concepts.name: Array with a complete Cartesian address set
concepts.gloss: An array whose addresses are all tuples in a product of ranges, stored in lexicographic order with the first coordinate most significant.

evidence.quote: is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant

concepts.name: Linear convolution
aliases: ordinary polynomial product of coefficient lists
concepts.gloss: The coefficient list of the ordinary product of two polynomials, with no reduction modulo any polynomial, so its length is the sum of the input lengths minus one.

concepts.name: Fixed tracks
concepts.gloss: Additional fixed rows of a tape that store extra data in parallel with the main data, so that a fixed number of tracks changes the running time only by a constant factor.

evidence.quote: Fixed tracks and finitely many work tapes change time by a fixed factor

concepts.name: Frankl–Wilson construction
aliases: Alon's presentation of the Frankl–Wilson construction
concepts.gloss: A construction of set systems with restricted intersection sizes, which gives low-degree polynomial representations of intersection graphs over fields.

evidence.quote: presentation of the Frankl–Wilson construction [9] gives low-degree representations of complementary intersection graphs over different fields

concepts.name: Gather and scatter operations
concepts.gloss: Operations that collect the entries of a network's wires over a three-element subset and redistribute them, producing coefficients that depend only on the size of the intersection of two subsets.

evidence.quote: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic numbers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are dyadic rationals, that is, have denominators that are powers of two.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Disk-grid values
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers stored exactly with p fractional bits in each real and imaginary part, with norm bounded by a fixed constant.

evidence.quote: Their coefficients are exact p-bit grid values of norm less than 1/4

concepts.name: Indicator vector
concepts.gloss: A vector indexed by a ground set whose entry is 1 at the elements of a given subset and 0 elsewhere.

concepts.name: Linear contraction
concepts.gloss: A linear map that does not increase the size of its inputs, so that its output has norm at most that of the input.

evidence.quote: The ordered Gaussian resampling maps are contractions

concepts.name: Normalized cost
concepts.gloss: The running time of an operation divided by the stored volume V, so that costs of different operations on arrays of different sizes can be compared as powers of p.

evidence.quote: Table 1 lists costs after division by V

concepts.name: Record
concepts.gloss: A fixed-width block of stored data, such as one polynomial with complex coefficients, that is handled as a single unit by the procedures.

evidence.quote: Each record is a polynomial with complex fixed-point coefficients

concepts.name: Row of an array
concepts.gloss: The block of consecutive entries that share a fixed prefix and row index, containing all address fields after the row field.

evidence.quote: regard a row as the complete ordered suffix, including all active address fields, at a fixed prefix and row index

concepts.name: Sup norm
concepts.gloss: The maximum absolute value of the coefficients of a polynomial or array.

evidence.quote: Both exact maps preserve the coefficient sup norm
